name: Washington
nameStory: The only state named for a US president - and it was an accident. Settlers wanted to call it Columbia. Congress changed it to Washington specifically to avoid confusion with the District of Columbia, thereby creating the single most confusing state name in the country.
capitalStory: Olympia is named for the Olympic Mountains you can see across Puget Sound, which were themselves named after Mount Olympus by a homesick English captain. The capital is named after a view.

majorFeatures.name: Cascade Range
majorFeatures.note: Volcanic wall splitting the state in two

majorFeatures.name: Puget Sound
majorFeatures.note: A drowned glacial trough full of islands

majorFeatures.name: Columbia River
majorFeatures.note: The border, the dams, and the salmon runs

funFacts: The Olympic Peninsula gets about 12 feet of rain a year while eastern Washington gets 8 inches. The Cascades wring out every Pacific storm, so one state contains a rainforest and a near-desert.
Mount St. Helens blew sideways on May 18, 1980, removing 1,300 feet of its own summit in minutes.
Grand Coulee Dam is the largest power-producing facility in the United States.
Rainier is considered the most dangerous volcano in America - not for lava, but for mudflows that would run down valleys where cities now sit.
whyItMatters: The government chose Hanford, on the Columbia River, to make plutonium for the Manhattan Project because it was isolated and had cold water and cheap dam power. The plutonium in the Nagasaki bomb was made there, and Hanford is now the most contaminated nuclear site in the Western Hemisphere.
